after: ## What the definition asks of you
alt: Section B offers four questions, two descriptive and two narrative, and one is answered in about 350 to 450 words for 25 marks. The definition splits into four targets: the subject, the atmosphere, specific detail and the reader picturing it; the piece is marked on W1, W2, W3 and W5, with W4 not assessed.
caption: Every phrase of the definition is a target, and four writing objectives carry the 25 marks.

alt: A check for the words “and then”: if you are still describing, a small event such as a gust of wind or a stall closing serves the picture; if not, the piece has drifted into narrative, like an answer that starts at a market and ends with a chase.
caption: Small events can serve a description; a plot that takes over cannot.

alt: Six ways to shape a description: zoom from a wide view to one detail, time-lapse of one place at dawn, noon and night, a journey from entrance to far corner, the senses in turn, before and after an interruption, and a circular piece that ends where it began with the mood changed.
caption: Pick a structure before you write; each paragraph becomes one stage of it.

alt: General words such as nice, busy, beautiful and lots of are replaced with specific nouns and precise verbs: food becomes skewers of charred corn, a bird becomes a crow, and the smoke went up becomes the smoke unravelled into the dark. Three further tools: selected senses, sparing figurative language and a single person in the scene.
caption: Swap the general word for the specific one the reader can see.

alt: A market at dawn described two ways: peaceful, with the first stallholder yawning and a cat stretching on a sack of rice, or unsettling, with shutters half-raised and a single light swinging. Light, weather, colour and sound are the strongest atmosphere tools.
caption: The place stays the same; the details you select make the mood.

alt: The railway station model moves in stages: one detail (a pigeon under the last light), the departure board reading Cancelled, the people on the benches, and the one-line paragraph “Then the cleaner arrives.” Notes beside each stage give the commentary’s points on precise pictures, the single chosen sense and light personification.
caption: A zoom structure: each stage is a paragraph, and the final small event opens the next.

alt: Spend about five minutes planning atmosphere, structure and details per stage, write four or five paragraphs aiming for the middle of 350 to 450 words, then proofread for W5. A sample plan built from the railway station model lists the atmosphere, a zoom structure and four stages.
caption: Five minutes of planning gives every paragraph its stage and its details.
